profile.reading: This facility is attributed in the registry to NTT, part of Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation, one of the largest telecommunications and IT services groups in the world, headquartered in Tokyo, Japan. NTT operates a global data center business, NTT Global Data Centers, built substantially through acquisitions; the one specific NTT data center acquisition confirmed this session was NTT Communications purchase of an 86.7 percent stake in e-shelter, described as Germany top data center operator, completed around June 23, 2015, though that acquisition is not directly connected to this United States facility. Multiple attempts this session to reach RagingWire, the United States data center company widely associated with NTT American operations, failed: the ragingwire.com domain could not be reached, and no corresponding Wikipedia article was found under the titles tried. NTT own corporate site returned only general Group level information rather than data center specific history. No building specific address, founding date, acquisition story, square footage, or MW figures for this United States facility were confirmed in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
NTT VA11 sits on 300,000 square feet of technical space in Gainesville, Virginia and publishes 96 MW of IT capacity. That figure places it third by published IT load among the 19 Virginia facilities this site has read with a stated megawatt figure, behind only two larger campuses in a state whose 19 published facilities sum to 1,326 MW. VA11's 96 MW represents roughly 7 percent of that published total. Virginia hosts 326 mapped facilities in aggregate, but the vast majority publish no capacity figure, so the true state total is larger and VA11's share of it is smaller than 7 percent.

Ninety-six megawatts of IT load is a substantial allocation by any current standard. As an assumption, at 10 kW per rack, a typical colocation density, 96 MW supports roughly 9,600 racks; at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, the same power supports roughly 2,400 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's claim. The 300,000 square feet of technical space works out to roughly 3.1 watts per square foot at the lower rack density assumption and roughly 320 watts per square foot at the higher one, which illustrates how strongly the usable AI capacity depends on the cooling and power delivery design NTT has not published here.

No certifications appear in the published specifications this site retrieved, so none can be read for what workloads they qualify. The campus address resolves to the Northern Virginia corridor, the densest data center market in the country by any published measure, which means grid interconnection, fiber diversity, and competitive supply are all plausible but not confirmed by the operator page. What the operator page does confirm is a campus large enough, at 96 MW, to matter to any enterprise or hyperscaler tenant whose AI workload demands continuous, high-density power at scale.
